displayedInputs.question: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle B=50^\circ\) and \(\angle C=70^\circ\). \(AD\) bisects \(\angle BAC\) and intersects \(BC\) at \(D\). Find the measure of \(\angle ADB\) in degrees.
The three angle bisectors of a triangle intersect at one point. Where is this point located?

choices.C: On a side of the triangle
choices.D: At a vertex of the triangle

displayedInputs.question: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle A=80^\circ\), \(BD\) bisects \(\angle ABC\), and \(CE\) bisects \(\angle ACB\). \(BD\) and \(CE\) intersect at point \(O\). Find the measure of \(\angle BOC\) in degrees.
Two angles of a triangle are \(50^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\). What is the third angle (unit: degrees)?
Of the three interior angles of a triangle, one is \(100^\circ\) and another is \(30^\circ\). How many degrees is the third interior angle?
The measures of the three interior angles of a triangle are in the ratio \(2:3:4\). Find the measure of the largest interior angle in degrees.
When proving that the interior angles of a triangle sum to \(180^\circ\), a line parallel to \(BC\) is drawn through vertex \(A\). Which fact is mainly used?

choices.A: When two lines are parallel, alternate interior angles are equal
choices.B: When two lines are parallel, interior angles on the same side of a transversal are supplementary
choices.D: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two nonadjacent interior angles

displayedInputs.question: One interior angle of an isosceles triangle is \(80^\circ\). What are the possible measures of its vertex angle in degrees? (List all possible values in ascending order, separated by commas.)
One acute angle of a right triangle is \(35^\circ\). What is the other acute angle (unit: degrees)?
One acute angle of a right triangle is \(62^\circ\). How many degrees is the other acute angle?
In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle A=40^\circ\) and \(\angle B=50^\circ\). What type of triangle is \(\triangle ABC\)?
The two acute angles of a right triangle differ by \(20^\circ\). How many degrees is the larger acute angle?
In right triangle \(ABC\), \(\angle ACB=90^\circ\), \(CD\perp AB\) at \(D\), and \(\angle A=35^\circ\). Find the measure of \(\angle BCD\) in degrees.
Two interior angles of a triangle are \(40^\circ\) and \(70^\circ\). What is the exterior angle adjacent to the third angle (unit: degrees)?
An exterior angle of a triangle equals:

choices.A: The interior angle adjacent to it
choices.B: The sum of the two interior angles nonadjacent to it
choices.C: The sum of the three interior angles
choices.D: The sum of the two interior angles adjacent to it

displayedInputs.question: In \(\triangle ABC\), point \(D\) lies on the extension of \(BC\). Given \(\angle ACD=130^\circ\) and \(\angle A=50^\circ\), find the measure of \(\angle B\) in degrees.

An exterior angle of a triangle measures \(120^\circ\). The ratio of the two interior angles that are not adjacent to it is \(1:3\). Find the measure of the larger of these interior angles in degrees.
In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle B=40^\circ\) and \(\angle C=60^\circ\). The bisector \(AD\) of \(\angle BAC\) intersects \(BC\) at \(D\). Find the measure of \(\angle ADC\) in degrees.
Which parts must be written when proving that “the sum of the exterior angles of a triangle is \(360^\circ\)”?
When writing the proposition “vertically opposite angles are equal” in the form “Given” and “To prove,” what should be written under “Given”?

In a proof, the statement “Since \(AB\parallel CD\) (\(\angle 1\) and \(\angle 2\) are alternate interior angles formed when lines \(AB\) and \(CD\) are cut by a third line), it follows that \(\angle 1=\angle 2\)” is based on:

choices.A: If two lines are parallel, their alternate interior angles are equal
choices.B: If alternate interior angles are equal, the two lines are parallel
choices.C: If two lines are parallel, their same-side interior angles are supplementary

displayedInputs.question: Every step in a geometric proof must have a justification. Which of the following cannot serve as a justification for reasoning?

choices.B: Definitions and theorems that have been learned

displayedInputs.question: When proving that “the sum of the exterior angles of a triangle is \(360^\circ\),” choose one exterior angle at each vertex of \(\triangle ABC\). At each vertex, the interior angle and exterior angle form a linear pair. What is the total sum, in degrees, of the interior and exterior angles at the three vertices?
Where is the center of gravity of a triangular thin plate?

choices.A: The intersection of the three altitudes
choices.B: The intersection of the three angle bisectors
choices.C: The intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of the three sides
choices.D: The intersection of the three medians

displayedInputs.question: To locate the center of gravity of a triangular thin plate using the suspension method, draw a line on the plate along the suspension string each time the suspended plate comes to rest. The center of gravity lies on these lines. What is the minimum number of times the plate must be suspended to determine the position of its center of gravity?
In a uniform triangular thin plate \(ABC\), \(AD\) is the median to side \(BC\), and \(BC=12\text{ cm}\). Find the length of \(BD\) (in cm).

A uniform triangular thin plate \(ABC\) is suspended from vertex \(A\). When it comes to rest, the suspension line (a vertical line) passes through the plate's center of gravity. Its intersection with side \(BC\) is:

choices.B: The foot of the perpendicular from \(A\) to \(BC\)
choices.C: The intersection of the bisector of \(\angle A\) with \(BC\)

displayedInputs.question: Given \(\triangle ABC\cong\triangle DEF\), which point corresponds to point \(A\)?
Which of the following statements is correct?

choices.A: Two triangles with equal areas are congruent
choices.B: Two triangles with equal perimeters are congruent
choices.C: Two figures that can be made to coincide exactly are congruent
choices.D: Two figures with the same shape are congruent

displayedInputs.question: Given \(\triangle ABC\cong\triangle CDE\), the side corresponding to \(AB\) is:

\(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DEF\) are congruent, with \(\angle A=\angle E\), \(\angle B=\angle D\), and \(\angle C=\angle F\). Write the congruence statement with corresponding vertices in order: △ABC≌△___ (fill in three letters).
Given \(\triangle ABC\cong\triangle DEF\) and \(AB=5\), what is the length of \(DE\)? (The vertices correspond as \(A\leftrightarrow D\), \(B\leftrightarrow E\), and \(C\leftrightarrow F\).)
Given \(\triangle ABC\cong\triangle DEF\) and \(\angle B=70^\circ\), what is the measure of \(\angle E\) in degrees?
Given \(\triangle ABC\cong\triangle DEF\), \(\angle A=40^\circ\), and \(\angle E=60^\circ\), find the measure of \(\angle C\) in degrees.
Given \(\triangle ABC\cong\triangle DEF\), \(AB=3\), \(BC=4\), and the perimeter of \(\triangle DEF\) is \(12\), find the length of \(AC\).
Given \(\triangle ABC\cong\triangle DEF\), \(AB=2x+1\), and \(DE=4x-7\), find the value of \(x\).
The corresponding sides of \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DEF\) are equal. Are they congruent? Which criterion applies?
Which of the following sets of conditions guarantees that \(\triangle ABC\cong\triangle DEF\)?

choices.C: \(\angle A=\angle D\), \(\angle B=\angle E\), \(\angle C=\angle F\)

displayedInputs.question: In \(\triangle ABC\) and \(\triangle DEF\), \(AB=DE\), \(AC=DF\), \(BC=2x+1\), and \(EF=13\). What must \(x\) equal for the triangles to be congruent by SSS?
In quadrilateral \(ABCD\), \(AB=CD\) and \(AD=CB\). Draw \(AC\). Which criterion establishes \(\triangle ABC\cong\triangle CDA\)?
